finding: the module's claim lines sit one constant away from the constants they describe (FORD carries POND_BERTH's and LANE_FT's claims, RUN_W carries JOIN_TRUNK's and REED_FT's, OFFTAKE_DEG carries the BROOK_* claims and BROOK_W's, WEIR_SKEW_DEG carries WEIR_KEY_FT's and field_in's, STANDOFF_FT carries BELT_FAR_FT's); the comments are probably placed below the constant where the bundler reads them as belonging to the one above
the inline CONVENTION notes for the reeds painted under the field and for the dashed settlement placeholder are comments, not Research claims, so no check sees them
nothing on how a brook wanders or slews down its valley, so the brook-course claim cites a page that does not bear on it
gives no weights for the winter crop's odds, so whether the code's fixed 0.5/0.5 is drift cannot be judged without the field build

it calls DIKE_CROPS, LEFTOVER_FORMS and FRY_FORMS GUESSes under a pointer to 0019, whose drawing page says nothing on dike crops, leftover parcels or fry ponds; the GUESS should stand on its own or name a page that records it
0031 §12 says a scattered settlement needs roughly twice the room per farm, but the band area does not vary with settlement_form; whether the seat/canvas room should account for that is unclaimed
five lane shapes are named (including a lane along the water), while the hamlet's lane_skeleton table carries four; the page does not say which of the five a hamlet may take

the module claim "the field's paint" cites 0007 (the wet-paddy tint), but no unit in svg.rs picks a paddy color, and every unit without its own claim inherits it; give the plumbing units NONE and move the 0007 claim to the code that picks the tint
the GUESS names no file; 0006 drawing §17 records this spacing as a guess, so the claim could cite that page
the reed fringe is recorded with no cut width or depth, so the 15 ft and 280 ft figures that rust/phases/src/driver/polder.rs carries have no guess recorded on the page
the module's "the polder" claim is inherited by ink constants and crown_fill, which should each carry a CONVENTION claim of their own
the polder's off-canvas test is a drawing convention that no claim of this unit names
the comment names `rules::held` as only the 25 degree and quarter-cell rules; it leaves out the arrowhead rule that `held` also applies
the sub-rule "a resting plot never its host" has no backing on 0008 or 0013; it could be stated as a GUESS

the fringe test gets flanks ['W','S'] for fall south and seat east, leaving the north flank bare. 0019 §80 says every flank but the landward one holds water back, and §79 puts the wild pond to the northwest. Check whether flanks() should also fringe a water-facing north flank.
the page does not record the hamlet rule for a declared fall that runs into the wind (keep the hill, seat off the wind; feature 444 T27, Sawada). It should be recorded as a GUESS.
the bundle does not show the sign convention of `wind` in margins::ranked, so I could not confirm that `wind = -fall` means "the wind came down from the high side", as the comment says.
the claim names four states (green, flooded, gold, at rest), but the code paints five: Wet takes FLOODED and Flooded takes POND_WATER; the claim should name the wet state
the kept ground runs only along `out`, at the band's own lateral width; 0072 §1/§3 lets a belt hold one windward side or two (a hook), and a second side's ground is not kept here
named and described as a "share", but it holds 31 ft, a length along the canal (row_ft x 31 = 1,488 sq ft); the claim's wording should say a length
these pages are cited by BROOK_TAP_RUN, OFFTAKE_DEG, draw_field and fill but were not in the bundle; the GUESS, CONVENTION and UNRESEARCHED verdicts rest on the pages that were

the account says "the page names no crop on the dikes", but 0019.drawing names "mulberry dikes" (§110) and vegetables grown "under the mulberry" (§113). Mulberry on the dikes is attested; only fruit, tea and the shares are a guess
0031.drawing §25 lists five lane forms including "a lane along the water"; the table carries four. The fifth is excluded only where §33's water condition fails, and the table never rolls it

the polder is centered at (w/2, h/2) and its split is fixed at 0.5 when it is not a dike-pond block; no claim covers either. They look like plumbing (the canvas middle, and a split this path does not use), but if the centring decides where the polder stands against the landward shore (§94), it wants a claim.

the claim cites research/questions/0031-clustered-and-scattered-villages-shuson-sanson.drawing.html, but the bundle does not include it under questions/; the bundle needs to ship it so the claim can be judged
